note: Runs are offline on purpose: Ableton allows one driver at a time (AGENTS.md rule 1), so subagents produce the note data they would send instead of touching Live. Assertions are computed by scratchpad measure.py from the note data alone.

evals.name: antitemplate
evals.prompt: fammi un beat hip hop sporco, ma che non sembri boom bap nostalgico — voglio che sia strano
evals.expected_output: A drum pattern (plus bass if warranted) that honours hip hop priors — pocket, space, hard backbeat weight — without reproducing the boom bap archetype. The point of this eval is that the correct answer is NOT the canonical pattern.
assertions: Drum pitches are all valid General MIDI drum numbers (35-81)
Velocities are all within 1-127 and no duplicate note occupies the same pitch and instant
Velocity is tiered rather than flat: at least 4 distinct values and a standard deviation above 12
Ghost notes are present: at least one drum hit below velocity 60
Timing is not fully quantised: at least one onset sits off the sixteenth grid, or an explicit swing/microtiming choice is described in the rationale

The result departs from the boom bap archetype in at least one measurable way (tempo outside 85-95, snare not exclusively on the 2/4 backbeat, unusual drum voices, or a non-standard subdivision) — this is the anti-template check
The rationale explains musical decisions in terms of dimensions (density, syncopation, accent, microtiming, register) rather than naming a genre template

evals.name: feeling-to-dimensions
evals.prompt: qualcosa di cupo e spoglio a 100, che respiri — batteria e basso, niente di piu'
evals.expected_output: A sparse, dark drums-and-bass pair at exactly 100 BPM where the sparseness is real (low density, audible gaps) and the kick and bass do not fight for the same instant.
assertions: Tempo is exactly 100, as the brief specified
Only drums and bass are present — no chord or melody clip was added beyond the brief
The pattern is genuinely sparse: drum density at or below 3 notes per beat, and at least one gap of a beat or more between consecutive onsets
Bass notes sit in the bass register (all below MIDI 55)
The kick and the bass do not collide: at most one bass onset lands on a kick instant
Velocity is tiered rather than flat: at least 4 distinct values in the drum clip
The rationale connects the words 'cupo', 'spoglio' and 'respiri' to concrete musical dimensions rather than to a genre

evals.name: harmonic-ambiguity
evals.prompt: accordi che non si capisce se sono tristi o allegri, sospesi, e sotto un basso che li tiene fermi
evals.expected_output: Chords that withhold the information which would settle major or minor — suspended, quartal, open fifths, or thirds deliberately absent — over a static or pedal bass.
assertions: Ambiguity is actually realised in the notes: the chord voicings omit the third, or use sus2/sus4/quartal/open-fifth structures, rather than being ordinary major or minor triads
Chord notes sit in a register that does not turn to mud (all chord tones at or above MIDI 48)
The bass holds still as the brief asked: it uses two or fewer distinct pitches, or repeats a single pitch as a pedal
Bass notes are below MIDI 55 and do not double the chord voicing in the same octave
Chords are voiced as simultaneous notes (at least 3 notes sharing a start time)
Velocities are all within 1-127 and no duplicate note occupies the same pitch and instant
The rationale explains the ambiguity in terms of a musical force (missing third, suspension, pedal, function withheld) rather than naming a chord progression from a style
